references.text: Parallel law text about piercing the ear of a slave who chooses to remain with his master forever, using an awl against the door.
The psalm refers to pierced ears as a sign of willing service and obedience, often interpreted messianically.
The use of הָאֱלֹהִים (elohim) in a legal context, where the case is brought before God or judges.
Another instance where אֱלֹהִים is used, possibly referring to judges or God in a legal context.
Mention of מְזוּזָה (doorpost) as an important place in Israelite households, where God's words were to be written.
Supplementary laws concerning the treatment of Hebrew slaves and their rights in the Year of Jubilee.
Theological contrast: The human servant's eternal service (as a sign) versus the enduring existence of David's house (God's promise).
